title: Why Your Production Schedule Is Wrong Before It Even Starts
description:
Production schedules look solid when they leave ERP, yet material delays, tool issues, missing skills and short machine stops make them outdated before the first order starts. This episode is for manufacturing planners, operations leaders and data architects who keep seeing Excel become the real control system. You will learn how a closed loop of execution data, production context, learning and controlled replanning keeps dispatch decisions feasible.
In this episode
00:00 – The familiar Friday afternoon scenario04:47 – A production schedule is a decision about the future09:34 – What ERP knows and where execution takes over17:46 – Measuring, context and learning from plan versus actual32:08 – Replanning, the closed loop and why Excel survives49:13 – Production context: machine stops, material, quality and finite capacity71:06 – Dashboards, Microsoft Fabric, OT data, digital twins and knowledge graphs88:52 – Industrial AI, the planner's role and event-driven replanning
Key takeaways
A released ERP schedule is a decision based on yesterday's facts, so it needs a closed feedback loop of execution, measurement, learning and replanning to stay feasible.Production events only become useful when they connect to order, operation, resource and time through explicit product, process and resource relationships, with shared definitions for words like complete and available.Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, digital twins, knowledge graphs and industrial AI can support the loop, but feasible replans still need explicit constraints, trigger rules, freeze windows and named human decision rights.
